chunks: 229 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah said: He narrated to me Abu al-Qasim Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'What is the ruling for a man who plays with his penis during the obligatory prayer?' He said, 'What is there for him to do?' I said, 'He played with it until he touched it with his hand,' so he said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm (it is permissible/does not invalidate)

ai.seo_question: Does touching or playing with the penis invalidate the obligatory prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that minor fidgeting or touching of the penis during obligatory prayer does not invalidate it, distinguishing it from actions that cause major distraction. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of leniency in cases of natural human impulses, provided the disruption is not significant enough to break the concentration (khushu) required for valid prayer.
